subject: Copywriting
title: Google AdWords Changed Everything
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Google AdWords Changed Everything.

hook.text: In 2000, Google launched AdWords. Advertisers bid on keywords and paid only when someone clicked.

buildup.text: For the first time, ads appeared when people searched for something specific. Intent met message perfectly.

discovery.text: AdWords forced extreme brevity: 25-character headlines, 70-character descriptions. Every word counted.

twist.text: Google made $200 billion in ad revenue by 2023. A text-only ad format outearned TV, radio, and print.

climax.text: Search ads proved that relevance beats creativity. The right words at the right moment outsell any jingle.

punchline.text: 25 characters. $200B in revenue. Words at the right moment.

quiz.question: What made Google AdWords revolutionary?
options: Ads shown based on search intent

details.summary: Google AdWords (now Google Ads), launched in 2000, revolutionized advertising by letting businesses show text ads to people actively searching for their products. Pay-per-click pricing, keyword targeting, and auction-based placement created a self-service advertising system that democratized...
details.whyItMatters: AdWords made copywriting a performance metric. Every word in a Google ad can be measured against clicks and conversions, creating the most accountable form of advertising copywriting ever invented.
takeaways: Google AdWords launched in 2000 as a self-service ad platform
Pay-per-click meant advertisers only paid when someone engaged
Search ads reached people at the exact moment of purchase intent

faq.question: Why did Google AdWords change advertising?
faq.answer: It targeted by intent, not demographics. Instead of guessing who might want your product, you showed ads to people actively searching for it. This made advertising more efficient, measurable, and accessible to small businesses.

faq.question: How did AdWords change copywriting?
faq.answer: Every headline and description competed in real-time auctions. Click-through rates directly affected cost and visibility. Copywriters had to write not just persuasively but measurably. A/B testing became continuous, and data replaced creative intuition as the primary decision tool.
